title: One captured password-reset link becomes permanent ownership of a TOTP-protected account, including its recovery address

steps.action: request a password reset for the victim's address, take the token from the mailbox and redeem it through the DDP resetPassword method, which is exempted from the second factor and returns a session
steps.result: a working login token for an account that enrolled TOTP, plus the password the attacker chose (the same account's password login still answers totp-required)

steps.action: call users.info for that session's own user id, which returns the stored services document
steps.result: the account's base32 TOTP seed (identical to the enrolled one) and its 12 backup-code hashes: the second factor, computable offline for ever

steps.ref: the account-settings email change and its second-factor step-up
steps.action: change the account's email address with users.updateOwnBasicInfo, satisfying the step-up that Rocket.Chat requires for that change with a code computed from the seed taken in step 2
steps.result: the account's recovery channel is the attacker's: a fresh anonymous forgotPassword mails the reset link to the attacker's mailbox, and the victim's own address no longer produces one

steps.action: hold the stolen token's DDP socket open across the victim's users.removeOtherTokens and the administrator's password reset
steps.result: the socket survives both remediations and receives the administrator's new password in clear, which logs in again together with a seed-derived code

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: from read access to one password-reset mail and nothing else, the attacker ends the run holding the account's password, its TOTP seed, and the email address every future recovery mail goes to, with its realtime session still open. Attacker capability before: read one message in a mailbox. After: full, permanent control of a 2FA-protected account whose owner cannot recover it through the product (their address is gone from the account), and which survives the two remediations the product offers short of deactivating the account: changing the password and logging out the other clients. The blast radius is one account per captured link, but any account, administrators included, and the hold does not decay.
preconditions: No Rocket.Chat account. Read access to one password-reset mail for the victim, or any capture of the link (a shared or archived mailbox, a forwarded message, a mail gateway log). The workspace runs its shipped configuration: no setting is changed by the attack or by the run. The victim has TOTP enrolled, which is what makes the chain interesting.
fix_order: Fix step 1: run the second-factor check on the recovery path (the resetPassword and verifyEmail login handlers behind VULN-015), so a reset either demands the enrolled factor or sets the password without returning a session. One change breaks the chain, because steps 2, 3 and 4 are all built on the session that step 1 hands out. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: a user with TOTP who resets their password must present a code or a backup code before being logged in, so someone who has lost both their password and their authenticator needs an administrator; the reset mail, the token and the password write are unchanged. The next most valuable fix is to project services out of users.info (VULN-004), which breaks steps 2 and 3 but leaves step 1's factor-free session standing.
